_note: The queries Pawprint's frontend actually makes, extracted from its code. A fix is only correct if every one of these still returns what the app expects.

flows.name: Alice loads her profile
flows.sql: select * from profiles where id = auth.uid()

flows.name: Alice sees her sitter's name on her booking
flows.sql: select p.full_name from bookings b join profiles p on p.id = b.sitter_id where b.owner_id = auth.uid()

flows.name: Alice lists her bookings
flows.sql: select * from bookings where owner_id = auth.uid()

flows.name: Alice creates a booking
flows.sql: insert into bookings (owner_id, sitter_id, pet_name, start_date, price_cents) values (auth.uid(), 'bbbbbbbb-0000-0000-0000-000000000002', 'Biscuit', '2026-12-01', 9000)

flows.name: Alice reads messages on her booking
Bob (sitter) sees both jobs assigned to him
flows.sql: select * from bookings where sitter_id = auth.uid()

flows.name: Bob replies on Alice's booking
flows.sql: insert into messages (booking_id, sender_id, body) values (1, auth.uid(), 'Got it, see you Saturday.')

isolation.name: Alice cannot read Carol's booking or door code
Alice cannot read Carol's phone or address
isolation.sql: select phone, home_address from profiles where id = 'cccccccc-0000-0000-0000-000000000003'

isolation.name: Alice cannot rewrite Carol's booking price
isolation.sql: update bookings set price_cents = 1 where owner_id = 'cccccccc-0000-0000-0000-000000000003' returning id

isolation.name: Alice cannot make herself a sitter
isolation.sql: update profiles set is_sitter = true where id = auth.uid() returning id

isolation.name: Alice cannot post as Bob
isolation.sql: insert into messages (booking_id, sender_id, body) values (1, 'bbbbbbbb-0000-0000-0000-000000000002', 'Fake reply from Bob')
